definition.simple: How many years of today's profit you pay for in the share price. Price ÷ earnings per share.
definition.balanced: P/E = share price ÷ [[eps]]. A high P/E means buyers expect profits to grow; a low P/E can mean low expectations, or a business in trouble. P/E says nothing on its own about whether a company is good, and it is meaningless when earnings are zero or negative.

example: Price 6.80 USD ÷ EPS 0.57 USD = a P/E of about 11.9.
